summary: mfa-js ships an import-time Windows dropper that fetches and persists a remote payload from limbomail.com
details: On require of mfa-js, index.js unconditionally loads./lib/cache, which on win32 downloads a JavaScript payload from https://limbomail.com/api/attachment/r_Ea6rT_kGfT.o7nh0aBVvDQWmOG47NPBQ3pUjd_uHeiw to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WinSxS\Backup\winsvc.js and executes it hidden via wscript.exe with a generated VBS wrapper. The module names child_process, https, spawn, wscript.exe,.vbs, attrib, schtasks, the HKCU registry paths, the Startup folder, and the limbomail.com URL are hex-escaped or base64-encoded to hide intent. After dropping the payload, four persistence mechanisms are installed so winsvc.js re-runs on every user logon: an HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run value named WinSvcHost, an HKCU\Environment UserInitMprLogonScript entry, a scheduled task \Microsoft\Windows\Shell\WinSvcHost with an onlogon trigger, and a wsvc.vbs shortcut in the user's Startup folder, with attrib +h +s used to hide the dropped files. The package is advertised as a Discord MFA helper and has no legitimate reason to fetch and execute remote code or install logon persistence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
